FAQ
Our Best Clients Had These Same Questions.
My score is already 800. Why would I need this?
A high score isn't the same as a file set up for the most funding. A name or address that doesn't match across the three bureaus can flag your file, and the report finds each one. Your business counts too: how old it is changes how much you can get, and the state it's in opens its own local banks. The roadmap lines up both sides in order, personal first, then the business.
Will this hurt my credit score?
No. We pull your credit with a soft inquiry. It doesn't show up on your report and your score doesn't move.
How do I know this is legit?
Gene went from the low 600s to 810 with these letters. Colin Schmidt, who ran a funding company, reviewed the roadmap and wouldn't change a thing. You can call us at (561) 304-8368 before you buy. And if you're not happy, email us within 7 days for a full refund.
How is this different from a funding course?
A course charges five to ten thousand dollars to teach you how to do it, and you dig the answers out yourself. This is the finished file. Every letter written, every step in order, built off your own credit.
How is this different from paying a broker?
A broker hands you a list of banks. This reads your own file first, fixes what's hurting it, and gives you the order to apply in so the declines don't stack.
What if my file needs a lot of work?
Then the roadmap says so and tells you how long. Some files need six months of dispute rounds. Some need two cards paid down. You'll know which one you are the day you open it.
Can you do the work for me?
No. This is do-it-yourself. You mail your own letters, so you hold every receipt and see every reply.
Can't I just apply on my own?
You can. Most people apply in the wrong order on a file nobody read, and each decline makes the next one harder. This tells you what to fix first and which banks to go to.
How fast do I get it?
About ten seconds after the soft pull finishes.
